$doc: Review queue (designed 2026-10-05): approvals queue one apply at a time per vault; after each apply waiting batches are re-checked and stale ones rebuilt (unapproved: before the owner looks; approved: rebuilt, then one more OK, decision A); exit 75 reads Updating, never a failure; bounded self-recovery (rules first, then a recovery model, default Opus); the batch tabs become a left list. boards.title: Review queue · approve several, they go in one at a time
boards.heading: Approve as many batches as you like: Distill adds them one at a time and keeps every plan current
boards.intro: “it is very bad, it list out each batch much better” and “when the issue happen it is nearly very difficult for the user to recover or fix the issue by itself, it will keep rerun and nothing will fix”. Approving a batch while another is being added queues it; applies run one at a time per vault, oldest approval first. After each apply the core re-checks every waiting batch against the vault. A stale batch you haven’t approved is rebuilt by its own session before you look (Updating…). A stale batch you approved is rebuilt and asks once more, with what changed since you approved: the approval gate binds every byte, so it never carries over (decision A). Exit 75 is never shown as a failure. A batch that still can’t move gets a bounded recovery: rules first, then a recovery model (Opus by default, set in Settings) that picks one fix the core can run and check, at most 2 times and $1.00, then “I couldn’t fix this” with your options. Review’s tabs become a list.
